answer: A voyage planner buys agents' maps of pearl farms in a lagoon. Each seller locks an external-asset bond per map through a fixed window for random audits by independent surveyors. Set audit probability p and forfeitable bond B so pB exceeds the maximum gain from a false map; hold the payout until the audit window ends. Splitting false maps across thousands of accounts preserves the audit odds per map and multiplies locked collateral, so cheap identities cannot lower the expected fraud cost. Surveyor independence and accurate ground truth are the trust assumptions.
